big_case.notes: The petition presents an acknowledged 5-1 circuit split (Eleventh Circuit against the First, Second, Seventh, Ninth, and Federal Circuits) on whether district courts may approve common-fund service or incentive awards to class representatives consistent with Trustees v. Greenough (1882) and Central Railroad & Banking Co. v. Pettus (1885) absent statutory or Rule 23 authorization. It drew a Call for a Response after initial waivers and an amicus brief from the U.S. Chamber of Commerce, making it doctrinally notable to class-action practitioners and repeat business litigants, though it concerns a technical civil-procedure question in a routine $5,000 award dispute with modest broader public salience.
